math.name: Mathematics
math.description: Core mathematical concepts aligned with Common Core Math Standards

count_to_100.name: Count to 100 by ones and tens
count_to_100.definition: Ability to count sequentially from 1 to 100 by ones, and count by tens to 100
learning_objectives: Count to 100 by tens starting at any number

one_to_one_correspondence.name: One-to-one correspondence
one_to_one_correspondence.definition: Understanding that each object in a set corresponds to exactly one number when counting
examples: Touching each toy once while counting: 1, 2, 3, 4, 5 toys
Matching one plate to each person at a table
common_misconceptions: Saying numbers without pointing to objects
learning_objectives: Touch each object once when counting
Understand the last number counted represents the total quantity

compare_numbers.name: Compare numbers
compare_numbers.definition: Identify whether a group of objects has more, less, or the same number as another group
examples: Which has more: 5 apples or 3 apples?
Do these groups have the same amount?
common_misconceptions: Confusing size of objects with quantity
Thinking spread out objects means more items
learning_objectives: Compare two groups using more, less, same

addition_within_5.name: Addition within 5
addition_within_5.definition: Solve addition problems with sums up to 5 using objects, fingers, or drawings
examples: I have 3 apples, you give me 2 more. How many do I have?
common_misconceptions: Not understanding addition means combining groups
Counting all objects from 1 instead of counting on
learning_objectives: Represent addition with objects and drawings

subtraction_within_5.name: Subtraction within 5
subtraction_within_5.definition: Solve subtraction problems within 5 using objects, fingers, or drawings
examples: I have 4 cookies and eat 1. How many are left?
common_misconceptions: Not understanding subtraction means taking away
Subtracting the smaller number from the larger regardless of order
learning_objectives: Represent subtraction with objects and drawings

addition_within_20.name: Addition within 20
addition_within_20.definition: Add numbers with sums up to 20 using strategies like counting on, making ten, and decomposing numbers
common_misconceptions: Always counting from one instead of counting on
Not recognizing making ten as an efficient strategy

subtraction_within_20.name: Subtraction within 20
subtraction_within_20.definition: Subtract numbers within 20 using strategies and understand relationship between addition and subtraction
common_misconceptions: Not understanding inverse relationship with addition
Always subtracting smaller from larger number

word_problems.name: Addition and subtraction word problems
word_problems.definition: Solve word problems that involve adding and subtracting within 20
examples: Sarah has 8 stickers. Tom gives her 5 more. How many does she have now?
There are 12 birds in a tree. 4 fly away. How many are left?
common_misconceptions: Not understanding what the question asks
learning_objectives: Identify relevant information in word problems
Write number sentences to represent problems

place_value.name: Number and Operations in Base Ten

place_value_tens_ones.name: Understanding place value (tens and ones)
place_value_tens_ones.definition: Understand that two-digit numbers represent amounts of tens and ones
examples: Ten ones can be thought of as one ten
common_misconceptions: Thinking '43' is just '4' and '3' next to each other
Not understanding the value of digit position
learning_objectives: Understand 10 can be thought of as a bundle of ten ones
Identify tens and ones in two-digit numbers

addition_within_100.name: Addition within 100
addition_within_100.definition: Fluently add within 100 using place value strategies and properties of operations

arrays_repeated_addition.name: Arrays and repeated addition
arrays_repeated_addition.definition: Work with equal groups to build foundation for multiplication using arrays and repeated addition
common_misconceptions: Not recognizing arrays as equal groups
learning_objectives: Use repeated addition for equal groups

place_value.name: Number and Operations in Base Ten

place_value_hundreds.name: Understanding place value to 1000
place_value_hundreds.definition: Understand that three-digit numbers represent amounts of hundreds, tens, and ones
common_misconceptions: Not understanding regrouping between place values
Thinking digits have the same value regardless of position
learning_objectives: Understand place value in three-digit numbers

multiplication_basics.name: Understanding multiplication
multiplication_basics.definition: Interpret products of whole numbers as total number of objects in equal groups

division_basics.name: Understanding division
division_basics.definition: Interpret quotients as number of objects in each share or number of shares
common_misconceptions: Not understanding division as inverse of multiplication

word_problems_mult_div.name: Multiplication and division word problems
word_problems_mult_div.definition: Solve two-step word problems using multiplication and division
examples: A baker makes 4 trays with 6 cookies each. He sells 8 cookies. How many are left?
24 students sit in 4 equal rows. How many students per row?

unit_fractions.name: Understanding unit fractions
unit_fractions.definition: Understand a fraction 1/b as the quantity formed by 1 part when a whole is partitioned into b equal parts
examples: 1/4 represents one part when something is divided into 4 equal parts
Pizza cut into 8 slices, one slice is 1/8
common_misconceptions: Thinking larger denominator means larger fraction
Not understanding parts must be equal

comparing_fractions.name: Comparing fractions
comparing_fractions.definition: Compare two fractions with same numerator or denominator by reasoning about their size
examples: 1/3 > 1/4 (same numerator, fewer parts means larger pieces)

multi_digit_multiplication.name: Multi-digit multiplication
multi_digit_multiplication.definition: Multiply multi-digit numbers using strategies based on place value and properties of operations
examples: Using area model or standard algorithm
common_misconceptions: Forgetting to add zeros as place holders

factors_multiples.name: Factors and multiples
factors_multiples.definition: Find factors and multiples of numbers, identify prime and composite numbers
learning_objectives: Find all factor pairs for numbers 1-100

equivalent_fractions.name: Equivalent fractions
equivalent_fractions.definition: Generate and recognize equivalent fractions using visual models and multiplication/division
examples: Multiply numerator and denominator by same number
common_misconceptions: Adding same number to numerator and denominator

adding_fractions.name: Adding and subtracting fractions
adding_fractions.definition: Add and subtract fractions with like denominators, including mixed numbers

multiplying_fractions.name: Multiplying fractions by whole numbers
multiplying_fractions.definition: Multiply a fraction by a whole number using visual models and equations
common_misconceptions: Not understanding it as repeated addition

decimal_fractions.name: Decimal notation for fractions
decimal_fractions.definition: Express fractions with denominators of 10 or 100 as decimals
common_misconceptions: Not understanding place value in decimals

place_value.name: Number and Operations in Base Ten

place_value_decimals.name: Place value with decimals
place_value_decimals.definition: Understand place value system extends to decimal places (tenths, hundredths, thousandths)
common_misconceptions: Thinking more decimal places means larger number
Not aligning decimal points when comparing
learning_objectives: Read and write decimals to thousandths

decimal_operations.name: Operations with decimals
decimal_operations.definition: Add, subtract, multiply, and divide decimals to hundredths
common_misconceptions: Not aligning decimal points in addition/subtraction

adding_unlike_denominators.name: Adding fractions with unlike denominators
adding_unlike_denominators.definition: Add and subtract fractions with unlike denominators by finding common denominators

multiplying_fractions_by_fractions.name: Multiplying fractions
multiplying_fractions_by_fractions.definition: Multiply fractions by fractions using area models and algorithms
learning_objectives: Understand product may be smaller than factors

dividing_fractions.name: Dividing with fractions
dividing_fractions.definition: Divide unit fractions by whole numbers and whole numbers by unit fractions
common_misconceptions: Not understanding division with fractions conceptually
Confusing when to invert and multiply
learning_objectives: Divide unit fractions by whole numbers
Divide whole numbers by unit fractions

volume_concepts.name: Understanding volume
volume_concepts.definition: Understand volume as attribute of 3D space, measured in cubic units
examples: Volume of box: length × width × height
Counting cubic units to find volume
learning_objectives: Measure volume by counting unit cubes

ratio_concepts.name: Understanding ratios
ratio_concepts.definition: Understand ratio as comparison of two quantities, use ratio language to describe relationships
examples: Ratio of boys to girls is 3:2 or 3 to 2 or 3/2
For every 3 cups of flour, use 2 cups of sugar
common_misconceptions: Not understanding order matters in ratios

unit_rates.name: Unit rates
unit_rates.definition: Find unit rates associated with ratios of quantities measured in different units
examples: 150 miles in 3 hours = 50 miles per hour

percent_concepts.name: Understanding percent
percent_concepts.definition: Understand percent as rate per 100, find percentages of quantities and solve percent problems

negative_numbers.name: Understanding negative numbers
negative_numbers.definition: Understand positive and negative numbers describe quantities in real-world contexts
examples: Temperature of -5°F means 5 degrees below zero
Bank account balance of -$20 means $20 in debt
common_misconceptions: Not understanding opposites on number line

integer_operations.name: Operations with integers
integer_operations.definition: Add, subtract, multiply, and divide integers using models and rules

rational_numbers.name: Rational numbers
rational_numbers.definition: Work with rational numbers (fractions, decimals, integers) on number line and in coordinate plane
common_misconceptions: Not understanding all integers are rational

algebraic_expressions.name: Writing and evaluating expressions
algebraic_expressions.definition: Write and evaluate numerical and algebraic expressions using order of operations
examples: Write expression: 5 more than twice a number = 2n + 5

solving_equations.name: Solving one-variable equations
solving_equations.definition: Solve one-step equations using inverse operations
common_misconceptions: Not performing same operation on both sides

reading.name: Reading/Language Arts
reading.description: Reading, writing, and language skills aligned with Common Core ELA Standards

print_concepts.name: Print concepts
print_concepts.definition: Understand that print carries meaning, follows left-to-right and top-to-bottom directionality
examples: Following words with finger while reading
Knowing where to start reading on a page
common_misconceptions: Starting to read from the right side
Not understanding that pictures and text are different

letter_recognition.name: Letter recognition
letter_recognition.definition: Recognize and name all upper and lowercase letters of the alphabet
examples: Find all the letter 'b's in a sentence

phonemic_awareness.name: Phonemic awareness
phonemic_awareness.definition: Demonstrate understanding of spoken words, syllables, and sounds (phonemes)
common_misconceptions: Not hearing individual sounds in words

letter_sounds.name: Letter-sound correspondence
letter_sounds.definition: Associate the long and short sounds with common spellings for the five major vowels and common consonants
common_misconceptions: Thinking each letter has only one sound

simple_words.name: Reading simple words
simple_words.definition: Read common high-frequency words by sight and decode simple CVC words
examples: Sight words: I, the, we, see, a
CVC words: cat, dog, sun, hop
common_misconceptions: Guessing based on first letter only

story_elements.name: Story elements
story_elements.definition: Identify characters, settings, and major events in a story

phonics_patterns.name: Phonics and word patterns
phonics_patterns.definition: Know and apply grade-level phonics including consonant blends, digraphs, and vowel patterns
examples: Blends: st, bl, gr (stop, blue, green)
Digraphs: sh, ch, th (ship, chin, then)
Long vowels: CVCe pattern (make, like, home)
common_misconceptions: Sounding out digraphs as two sounds
learning_objectives: Decode words with blends and digraphs

fluency.name: Reading fluency
fluency.definition: Read grade-level text with sufficient accuracy, appropriate rate, and expression

key_details.name: Identifying key details
key_details.definition: Ask and answer questions about key details in a text
examples: Finding evidence in text to answer
common_misconceptions: Making up answers not supported by text

characters_lessons.name: Characters and lessons
characters_lessons.definition: Describe characters and explain what lesson or moral the story teaches
examples: The story teaches us to be kind
common_misconceptions: Not connecting character actions to traits

advanced_phonics.name: Advanced phonics patterns
advanced_phonics.definition: Decode words with advanced patterns including vowel teams, r-controlled, and common suffixes
examples: Vowel teams: ai, ea, oa (rain, team, boat)
R-controlled: ar, or, er (car, fork, her)

story_structure.name: Story structure
story_structure.definition: Describe how stories have beginning, middle, and end; understand sequence of events

characters_compare.name: Comparing characters
characters_compare.definition: Compare and contrast characters, settings, or events in stories
examples: How are these two characters alike and different?
common_misconceptions: Only identifying similarities or only differences

theme.name: Theme and central message
theme.definition: Determine the theme or central message and explain how it is conveyed through key details
examples: Supporting details show characters helping each other

character_actions.name: Character traits and motivations
character_actions.definition: Describe characters and explain how their actions contribute to the sequence of events
examples: Character is determined, which leads to...
learning_objectives: Trace cause and effect of actions

figurative_language.name: Figurative language
figurative_language.definition: Distinguish literal from non-literal language and understand similes and metaphors
examples: Simile: as brave as a lion

main_idea.name: Main idea and supporting details
main_idea.definition: Determine main idea of text and explain how it is supported by key details
examples: Main idea: Dolphins are intelligent animals
Supporting details: they communicate, use tools, solve problems
common_misconceptions: Listing details without identifying main idea

opinion_writing.name: Opinion writing
opinion_writing.definition: Write opinion pieces with reasons supporting the opinion
examples: I think recess should be longer because...
My favorite season is summer. First reason..., second reason...

narrative_writing.name: Narrative writing
narrative_writing.definition: Write narratives with details describing actions, thoughts, and feelings
examples: Personal narratives with beginning, middle, end

inferencing.name: Making inferences
inferencing.definition: Refer to details and examples when explaining what text says explicitly and when making inferences
examples: The character slammed the door. (Infer: they are angry)
Using text clues plus background knowledge

theme_summary.name: Theme and summary
theme_summary.definition: Determine theme from details and summarize the text
examples: Summary: main events in order without opinion
common_misconceptions: Including too many details in summary

text_structure.name: Text structure
text_structure.definition: Describe overall structure of events, ideas, concepts, or information in a text
examples: Cause and effect: because, as a result

text_features.name: Using text features
text_features.definition: Interpret information from charts, graphs, diagrams, timelines, and other visual elements
examples: Reading information from a bar graph
Using diagram labels to understand content
learning_objectives: Use text features to locate information

context_clues.name: Using context clues
context_clues.definition: Determine meaning of unknown words using context clues
examples: Definition clues: enormous, which means very large
Example clues: vehicles such as cars, trucks, and buses

quote_text.name: Quoting accurately
quote_text.definition: Quote accurately from text when explaining what text says explicitly and when making inferences
examples: According to the text, "the storm grew fiercer."

compare_stories.name: Comparing stories
compare_stories.definition: Compare and contrast stories in the same genre on their approaches to themes and topics
examples: Both stories are about friendship but approach it differently...
common_misconceptions: Not analyzing how theme is developed

multiple_accounts.name: Analyzing multiple accounts
multiple_accounts.definition: Analyze multiple accounts of same event or topic, noting similarities and differences in point of view
examples: Comparing two articles about same historical event
common_misconceptions: Not recognizing author's point of view
Thinking there's only one correct account

argumentative_writing.name: Argumentative writing
argumentative_writing.definition: Write opinion pieces with logically ordered reasons supported by facts and details
examples: Claim: Schools should have longer lunch periods
Supporting with facts, examples, and expert opinions

research_writing.name: Research and informative writing
research_writing.definition: Conduct short research projects and write informative texts with facts, definitions, and details
examples: Using multiple sources to gather information

textual_evidence.name: Citing textual evidence
textual_evidence.definition: Cite textual evidence to support analysis of what text says explicitly and implicitly
examples: The text suggests... because it states...
Evidence: direct quotes and paraphrased ideas

plot_development.name: Analyzing plot development
plot_development.definition: Describe how plot unfolds in series of episodes and how characters respond or change
examples: Exposition, rising action, climax, falling action, resolution
learning_objectives: Understand cause and effect in plots

point_of_view.name: Point of view
point_of_view.definition: Explain how author develops point of view of narrator or speaker

central_idea.name: Central idea and summary
central_idea.definition: Determine central idea and how it is conveyed through details; provide objective summary
examples: Central idea: renewable energy is the future
common_misconceptions: Including too much detail in summary

author_purpose.name: Author's purpose and argument
author_purpose.definition: Determine author's purpose and analyze how it is conveyed; evaluate arguments and claims
examples: Evaluating strength of claims and evidence

argument_writing.name: Argument writing
argument_writing.definition: Write arguments to support claims with clear reasons and relevant evidence
examples: Claim with supporting reasons and evidence
common_misconceptions: Using emotional appeals instead of logic

science.name: Science
science.description: Elementary science concepts covering life, physical, and earth sciences

living_nonliving.name: Living vs. non-living things
living_nonliving.definition: Understand characteristics that distinguish living from non-living things
examples: Living: grow, need food/water, reproduce (plants, animals)
common_misconceptions: Thinking things that move are always alive
Thinking plants aren't alive because they don't move

animal_needs.name: Animal needs
animal_needs.definition: Understand that animals need food, water, and shelter to survive
examples: All animals need food for energy
common_misconceptions: Not understanding all animals have same basic needs
Thinking animals get needs in same way
learning_objectives: Explain why animals need these things
Describe how animals meet their needs

plant_needs.name: Plant needs
plant_needs.definition: Understand that plants need sunlight, water, and air to grow
examples: Plants need sunlight to make food

life_cycles.name: Life cycles
life_cycles.definition: Understand that living things have life cycles: born, grow, reproduce, die
common_misconceptions: Thinking all animals have same life cycle

properties_matter.name: Properties of matter
properties_matter.definition: Observe and describe properties of objects: size, shape, color, texture, weight
examples: Describing a ball: round, red, smooth, light
common_misconceptions: Not recognizing objects can have multiple properties

push_pull.name: Pushes and pulls
push_pull.definition: Understand that pushes and pulls can change how objects move
examples: Pushing a swing makes it go
Pulling a wagon makes it move
Stronger pushes make things go faster/farther
common_misconceptions: Not recognizing force is needed for motion
Thinking objects move on their own

weather.name: Weather and seasons
weather.definition: Observe and describe weather patterns and seasonal changes
examples: Types of weather: sunny, rainy, cloudy, snowy
Four seasons: spring, summer, fall, winter
common_misconceptions: Thinking weather and climate are the same
Not understanding seasons differ by location

earth_materials.name: Earth materials
earth_materials.definition: Identify different types of earth materials: rocks, soil, water, sand
examples: Soil is made of broken rocks and organic matter
Water in different forms: liquid, ice
common_misconceptions: Thinking all rocks are the same
Not understanding soil contains once-living things

adaptations.name: Adaptations
adaptations.definition: Understand that organisms have structures and behaviors that help them survive in their environment
examples: Polar bear's thick fur for cold climate
Birds have different beak shapes for different foods
common_misconceptions: Not understanding adaptations develop over time

food_chains.name: Food chains and webs
food_chains.definition: Understand how energy flows from sun to plants to animals in ecosystems
common_misconceptions: Not understanding energy comes from sun

ecosystems.name: Ecosystems and habitats
ecosystems.definition: Understand that organisms live in habitats that provide their needs and interact with other organisms
examples: Forest ecosystem: trees, deer, owls, insects
common_misconceptions: Thinking removing one species doesn't affect others

states_of_matter.name: States of matter
states_of_matter.definition: Understand that matter exists in different states: solid, liquid, gas
examples: Gases spread out to fill space
common_misconceptions: Not understanding particles are always present
Thinking matter disappears when it changes state

energy.name: Energy and motion
energy.definition: Understand that energy causes motion and heat, and can transfer between objects
examples: Heat energy transfers from hot to cold

simple_machines.name: Simple machines
simple_machines.definition: Understand how simple machines make work easier by changing force or direction
examples: Wheel and axle: doorknob, car wheel
common_misconceptions: Not recognizing simple machines in everyday objects

earth_systems.name: Earth's systems
earth_systems.definition: Understand Earth has different systems: geosphere, hydrosphere, atmosphere, biosphere

water_cycle.name: Water cycle
water_cycle.definition: Understand how water moves through Earth's systems: evaporation, condensation, precipitation
examples: Collection: water returns to bodies of water
common_misconceptions: Thinking water disappears when it evaporates

rocks_soil.name: Rocks and soil formation
rocks_soil.definition: Understand how rocks form and break down, and how soil is formed from weathered rock and organic matter
examples: Three rock types: igneous, sedimentary, metamorphic
common_misconceptions: Not understanding time scale of processes

solar_system.name: Solar system
solar_system.definition: Understand basic structure of solar system: sun, planets, moons, orbits
examples: Sun is a star at center
Inner planets (rocky): Mercury, Venus, Earth, Mars
Outer planets (gas giants): Jupiter, Saturn, Uranus, Neptune
common_misconceptions: Not understanding scale of solar system

social_studies.name: Social Studies
social_studies.description: Elementary social studies covering community, geography, history, and civics
social_studies.standards_framework: National Council for the Social Studies (NCSS)

family_community.name: Families and communities
family_community.definition: Understand that people live in families and communities with shared characteristics
common_misconceptions: Thinking all families are the same

rules_responsibilities.name: Rules and responsibilities
rules_responsibilities.definition: Understand that rules help people get along and everyone has responsibilities
examples: Being a good citizen: helping, sharing, taking turns
common_misconceptions: Thinking rules are just to restrict

maps_globes.name: Maps and globes
maps_globes.definition: Understand that maps and globes represent places and how to use basic map features

locations.name: Location and place
locations.definition: Describe location using positional words and understand places have characteristics
examples: Near, far, left, right, above, below

time_sequence.name: Time and sequence
time_sequence.definition: Understand concepts of past, present, future and sequence of events

personal_history.name: Personal and family history
personal_history.definition: Understand own history and how families have histories and traditions
common_misconceptions: Thinking past was exactly like present

continents_oceans.name: Continents and oceans
continents_oceans.definition: Identify and locate seven continents and major oceans on maps and globes
examples: 7 continents: North America, South America, Europe, Asia, Africa, Australia, Antarctica
5 oceans: Pacific, Atlantic, Indian, Arctic, Southern
learning_objectives: Label continents and oceans on map

map_skills.name: Advanced map skills
map_skills.definition: Use map components: compass rose, scale, legend, latitude/longitude
examples: Cardinal directions: N, S, E, W
Intermediate directions: NE, SE, SW, NW

regions_landforms.name: Regions and landforms
regions_landforms.definition: Identify different types of landforms and understand regions share common characteristics
examples: Landforms: mountains, plains, plateaus, valleys, deserts
Bodies of water: rivers, lakes, oceans
common_misconceptions: Not understanding how landforms affect climate

native_americans.name: Native Americans
native_americans.definition: Understand Native Americans were first inhabitants of America with diverse cultures
common_misconceptions: Stereotyping all Native Americans as the same
Using past tense (they still exist today)

exploration_colonization.name: European exploration and colonization
exploration_colonization.definition: Understand why and how Europeans explored and colonized the Americas
examples: Reasons for exploration: trade, resources, religious freedom

american_revolution.name: American Revolution
american_revolution.definition: Understand causes and key events of American independence from Britain
examples: Key events: Boston Tea Party, Declaration of Independence (1776)
Important figures: George Washington, Thomas Jefferson
common_misconceptions: Not understanding it was a civil war aspect

government_purpose.name: Purpose of government
government_purpose.definition: Understand government makes and enforces laws to maintain order and protect rights
common_misconceptions: Not understanding difference between laws and rules
Thinking government is just the president

branches_government.name: Three branches of government
branches_government.definition: Understand U.S. government has three branches with different roles
common_misconceptions: Thinking one branch has all power

citizenship.name: Rights and responsibilities of citizens
citizenship.definition: Understand citizens have both rights and responsibilities in a democracy
examples: Rights: freedom of speech, religion, assembly
Responsibilities: voting, obeying laws, paying taxes
Ways to participate: voting, volunteering, staying informed
learning_objectives: Identify rights in Bill of Rights

goods_services.name: Goods and services
goods_services.definition: Understand difference between goods (products) and services (actions people do for others)
common_misconceptions: Not understanding everyone is both producer and consumer

supply_demand.name: Supply and demand
supply_demand.definition: Understand basic concept that prices are affected by supply and demand
examples: High demand + low supply = higher prices
Low demand + high supply = lower prices
Example: toy in high demand before holidays
common_misconceptions: Not understanding relationship between supply and demand
